scope: JEP expert annotation, disagreement, active learning and meaningful participation
status: bounded critical review; not exhaustive systematic review

sources.citation: Barbara Plank. 2022. The ‘Problem’ of Human Label Variation: On Ground Truth in Data, Modeling and Evaluation. EMNLP.
sources.data_language: No new empirical JEP dataset; examples and surveyed NLP tasks.
sources.label_authority: Distinguishes plausible human variation from errors.
sources.method_result_limit: Argues aggregation can hide meaningful variation; number-of-items versus number-of-annotators tradeoff remains open. This is conceptual guidance, not general evidence of improved annotation efficiency.
sources.jep_gap: Validate reason-coded source uncertainty versus substantive disagreement; retaining disagreement itself is prior art.
sources.confidence: high for prior-art boundary; moderate for local empirical gap

sources.citation: Eve Fleisig, Su Lin Blodgett, Dan Klein, Zeerak Talat. 2024. The Perspectivist Paradigm Shift: Assumptions and Challenges of Capturing Human Labels. NAACL.
sources.data_language: No new benchmark; discusses cross-task human labeling.
sources.label_authority: Expertise, lived experience and demographic attributes are distinct; demographics do not fully determine perspectives.
sources.method_result_limit: Examines causal assumptions and normative choices behind perspectivist labels. Quality controls remain necessary; demographic inference cannot establish an individual's view.
sources.jep_gap: Specify who can correct factual errors, interpret a rubric or contest normative judgments; do not use expert-pool consensus as representative victim consent.

sources.citation: Nan-Jiang Jiang and Marie-Catherine de Marneffe. 2022. Investigating Reasons for Disagreement in Natural Language Inference. TACL.
sources.label_authority: Human NLI annotations; ambiguity and guideline interpretation analyzed separately from annotator behavior.
sources.method_result_limit: Ten reason categories in three broader classes; compares categorical complicated-case treatment with multilabel/distribution modeling. Multilabel treatment represents plausible interpretations better in this task. NLI inference is not restorative adequacy.
sources.jep_gap: Code whether disagreement arises from unavailable evidence, competing defensible inferences, rubric wording or substantive moral interpretation.

sources.citation: Xinpeng Wang and Barbara Plank. 2023. ACTOR: Active Learning with Annotator-specific Classification Heads to Embrace Human Label Variation. EMNLP.
sources.data_language: English HS-Brexit and Gab Hate Corpus; dense and sparse repeated binary hate-speech labels.
sources.label_authority: Existing individual annotator labels, not JEP experts.
sources.method_result_limit: Shared encoder and annotator-specific heads select item–annotator pairs using individual/group entropy and other acquisitions. Group entropy is strong but results vary by dataset and metric. Savings concern simulated label budgets, not observed expert minutes.
sources.jep_gap: Benchmark measured time and evidence-check effort for Spanish directed harm-response judgments, preserving role-specific disagreement.

sources.citation: Connor Baumler, Anna Sotnikova and Hal Daumé III. 2023. Which Examples Should be Multiply Annotated? Active Learning When Annotators May Disagree. Findings ACL.
sources.data_language: English Measuring Hate Speech and Wikipedia Talk; repeated ordinal labels.
sources.label_authority: Previously collected annotations replayed as simulated oracle responses.
sources.method_result_limit: DAAL selects mismatch between task-model entropy and predicted annotator entropy, permits repeat annotation, and evaluates label-distribution JS divergence. Beats ordinary uncertainty sampling in studied settings; authors explicitly limit evidence to simulations, English toxicity and existing quality controls.
sources.jep_gap: A baseline to beat, not a novel idea to rename. Test time/burden and reason-coded uncertainty prospectively, with fixed blind family-held-out audit data.

sources.citation: Robbie Haertel, Eric Ringger, Kevin Seppi, James Carroll and Peter McClanahan. 2008. Assessing the Costs of Sampling Methods in Active Learning for Annotation. ACL Short.
sources.label_authority: Existing POS reference labels; hourly cost estimates informed by a separate user study.
sources.method_result_limit: Compares random, query-by-committee, uncertainty and sequence-length acquisitions under sentence, word, correction and time costs. Acquisition ranking changes with the cost model. Transfer of the timing model and correction-cost assumptions is task dependent.
sources.jep_gap: Use expert-minutes including evidence reading, context switches and correction; fewer annotated pairs alone cannot support a productivity claim.

sources.citation: Eric Ringger et al. 2008. Assessing the Costs of Machine-Assisted Corpus Annotation Through a User Study. LREC.
sources.sections: §2 design, especially §2.4 and §2.6; §3 timing; §4 cost models
sources.data_language: English WSJ/Penn Treebank POS; word versus sentence annotation and controlled preannotation accuracy.
sources.label_authority: Study participants largely undergraduate syntax students, not JEP legal/trauma experts.
sources.method_result_limit: Measures timing under annotation granularity, preannotation accuracy and skill conditions. Shows why interface and error-correction costs must be measured. Restricted sentence lengths and grammatical tagging limit transfer to long testimony.
sources.jep_gap: Randomize source-only versus evidence-card or LLM-proposal assistance; measure both time and unsupported inferences/anchoring.

sources.citation: Mitchell Gordon et al. 2022. Jury Learning: Integrating Dissenting Voices into Machine Learning Models. CHI.
sources.sections: §4 model/data; §5 juries; §6 evaluation and §6.1.3 limitations; §7 moderator study
sources.data_language: English social-media toxicity; individual crowd ratings; moderator jury-composition study.
sources.label_authority: Individual annotator ratings; explicitly selected juries govern model aggregation.
sources.method_result_limit: Combines text and annotator representations to predict individual responses and composed juries. Conditional perspectives and dissent-aware outputs already exist. Information sharing can erase individual/intersectional perspectives; predicted views are not actual consultation.
sources.jep_gap: Keep observed expertise and affected-person perspectives separate; no virtual victim model can replace participation.

sources.citation: Fabrizio Gilardi, Meysam Alizadeh and Maël Kubli. 2023. ChatGPT outperforms crowd workers for text-annotation tasks. PNAS.
sources.data_language: Four English tweet/news samples, 6,183 documents; relevance, stance, topics and frames.
sources.label_authority: Trained research-assistant codebooks/reference labels; comparison with MTurk and repeated ChatGPT runs.
sources.method_result_limit: Zero-shot ChatGPT generally exceeds MTurk agreement with trained-coder references in these tasks. Repeated-model consistency is not independent human agreement. Multilingual transfer and other settings are explicitly future research, not demonstrated JEP validity.
sources.jep_gap: Treat LLM labels as untrusted proposals or separate synthetic supervision; expert source-grounding audit determines usefulness.

sources.citation: Harini Suresh, Emily Tseng, Meg Young, Mary Gray, Emma Pierson and Karen Levy. 2024. Participation in the Age of Foundation Models. FAccT.
sources.sections: §3 participatory ceiling; §4.1.2 domain subfloor; §4.1.3 application surface; §5.3 burden
sources.data_language: No new benchmark or completed intervention trial; clinical, journalism and finance examples are hypothetical.
sources.label_authority: Affected communities and domain participants can shape governance/task choices rather than only supply labels.
sources.method_result_limit: Maps different opportunities for participation across foundation-model development. Addresses burden, refusal and control; it does not demonstrate an annotation-efficiency intervention.
sources.jep_gap: Let participation change or reject the application and rubric. Valentina's expert pool alone does not establish representative victim participation.

sources.citation: Mijke de Waardt and Sanne Weber. 2019. Beyond Victims’ Mere Presence: An Empirical Analysis of Victim Participation in Transitional Justice in Colombia. Journal of Human Rights Practice 11(1):209–228.
sources.sections: Accepted manuscript introduction p4; Victim participation in practice pp19–30; Conclusions pp30–32
sources.data_language: Colombian Victims' Law implementation; interviews, focus groups, participant observation in municipal settings and two Caribbean communities; article English, fieldwork language not verified.
sources.label_authority: Victims, representatives and state/civil-society stakeholders; qualitative accounts, not a reusable NLP gold set.
sources.method_result_limit: Fieldwork from 2015–17 shows formal participation can impose time/work burdens, obscure representation and fail to create ownership. Context is nonjudicial Victims' Law implementation, not direct evaluation of present JEP NLP.
sources.jep_gap: Measure burden and agency, not attendance or labels alone. Preserve existing organizational channels and allow refusal rather than adding another extractive consultation exercise.

limits: No prospective JEP annotation experiment executed by this reviewer.
No expert availability, consent, human labels or hour savings assumed.
DOI null means not separately verified, not absent.
Primary-body sections inspected through publisher/author-hosted text; report distinguishes conceptual and empirical evidence.
Internal cached PDFs must not be included in GitHub publication.
